title: Tutorial Tours run as a modal on whatever screen you are on and tell you to click tabs that are not there -- and the modal blocks every one of them
summary: Closed by wave 4, which landed after the live re-verification (verifier shots timestamped 2026-08-03 17:xx; the fix files are dated 2026-08-03 23:19-23:25). I re-checked all three causes in the tree rather than assuming. (1) Navigation: packages/skotiq_app/lib/widgets/tutorial_overlay.dart:281 `_navigateForStep(context, steps[current.currentStepIndex]);` inside the tutorialProvider listener, resolving through packages/skotiq_app/lib/widgets/tutorial_overlay/tutorial_routes.dart:45 `tutorialRouteForStep` -- TutorialCategory.equipmentSetup maps to '/equipment' at tutorial_routes.dart:19. (2) Blocking: packages/skotiq_app/lib/widgets/tutorial_overlay/spotlight.dart:85 `if (_targetRect == null) return false;` (was: add BoxHitTestEntry + return true) and spotlight.dart:128-129 in _SpotlightPainter.paint, which now returns before drawing the full-screen dim when there is no target. (3) Copy/targets: the four Equipment Setup steps at packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/models/tutorial/tutorial_models_parts/onboarding_definitions.dart:274-327 no longer say 'Click the Profiles tab'/'Click the Connections tab'; they name the Profiles panel, its + button, Connect All and the device cards, and all four targetKeys now resolve to attached widgets (equipment_screen.dart:183 profileSelector, profile_sidebar.dart:133 createProfileBtn, profile_sidebar.dart:301 quickConnectBar, progress_dashboard.dart:382 cameraCard). The verifier's side observation ('the row still reads Not started while the tour is running') is moot now that starting the tour leaves the Settings screen.
revert_check: I ran both reverts myself, independently of wave 4's claim. (a) Commented out `_navigateForStep(context, steps[current.currentStepIndex]);` at tutorial_overlay.dart:281 => 'starting a tour opens the screen the tour is about' FAILED with Expected '/equipment', Actual '/settings'. (b) Restored alone (with the navigation line back in place) `if (_targetRect == null || !_isInteractive) { result.add(BoxHitTestEntry(this, position)); return true; }` at spotlight.dart:85 => 'an un-anchored step does not swallow clicks on the app' FAILED with Expected: contains 'EQUIPMENT', Actual: []. Both restored; 4/4 green.
caveats: Wave 4's caveat still stands and I did not widen it: only the Equipment Setup tour's step text was re-audited against current controls. The other tours now open on the right screen and no longer block the app, but e.g. tp_planetarium still targets 'nav_planetarium', and TutorialKeys.navPlanetarium/navFraming/navFlatWizard/navWeather are declared in tutorial_overlay.dart:46-50 but attached to no widget (app_shell.dart:869-878 attaches only sideNavigation/dashboard/equipment/imaging/sequencer/guiding/planner/analytics). Those steps therefore spotlight nothing -- but thanks to (2) they are now a floating card over a usable app rather than a barrier.

title: Paired devices always say 'Not seen yet / No connection recorded yet' -- last_connected_at is never written
summary: Closed by wave 4 (apps/desktop/test/headless_api_server/paired_device_last_seen_test.dart is dated 2026-08-03 22:04, after the 17:xx re-verification). The verifier's root cause was exact: PairingDatabase.updateLastConnected (packages/skotiq_remote_protocol/lib/src/database/pairing_database.dart:138) is only reached via TokenManager.verifySessionToken (token_manager.dart:297), which the desktop HTTP auth path never called because it resolves paired bearers against the in-memory BoundedTokenGrantMap. The tree now calls it from both places that recognise a paired token: apps/desktop/lib/headless_api_server/http_middleware.dart:847 `_touchPairedDeviceSeen(token);` immediately after `_tokenResolver.clearFailures(clientKey)` on the bearer path, and http_middleware.dart:678 `_touchPairedDeviceSeen(queryToken);` on the legacy ?token= WS upgrade. _touchPairedDeviceSeen (http_middleware.dart:1062) is fire-and-forget, per-token throttled, bounded against _pairedSessionTokens.maxEntries, and stamps through TokenManager.verifySessionToken rather than writing the column, so a credential the pairing layer would reject cannot be recorded as seen. I checked the read side too, since the finding is about what the screen says: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/pairing_screen.dart:713-725 and :830 read device.lastConnectedAt off rows loaded from the DB in PairingNotifier._initialize (pairing_screen.dart:116 _tokenManager.getActivePairedDevices), so the write is what the badge and subtitle are reading -- no second cache in between. The modern WS path is covered without a third call site: a client using POST /api/ws/ticket + ?ticket= authenticates that POST with its bearer, which goes through :847.
test: apps/desktop/test/headless_api_server/paired_device_last_seen_test.dart -- 2/2 green as found (real in-memory PairingDatabase, real started HeadlessApiServer, real authenticated GET /api/status).
revert_check: Commented out the production call site `_touchPairedDeviceSeen(token);` at apps/desktop/lib/headless_api_server/http_middleware.dart:847 => 'an authenticated request records the device as seen' FAILED with Expected: not null / Actual: <null> ('The device just made an authenticated request; the Paired Devices screen must not still read "Not seen yet".'). Restored; 2/2 green.
caveats: The finding's secondary ask -- surfacing the peer IP and model so the seven identically-named 'Android companion' rows can be told apart -- is NOT done. last_connected_at now distinguishes a live phone from a stale credential, which is the part the title and the repro are about, but two devices seen in the same window still render identically.

title: 'Active Viewers' on the Remote Access page counts co-imaging collaborators, not connected remote clients -- it stays 0 with a live dashboard socket open
summary: Closed by wave 4 (apps/desktop/test/headless_api_server/connected_client_count_test.dart dated 2026-08-03 23:50, after the 17:xx re-verification). The prior wave before that had only RELABELLED the row, which is why this carries prior_attempt=partial; the tree now publishes the number the page is actually asked about. Server: apps/desktop/lib/headless_api_server.dart:871 `int get connectedClientCount => _sockets.length;` with apps/desktop/lib/headless_api_server.dart:879 _publishConnectedClientCount emitted from the only three places _sockets changes -- websocket_sessions.dart:82 (attach), websocket_sessions.dart:138 (drop) and server_lifecycle.dart:759 (shutdown clear). GUI: apps/desktop/lib/desktop_app_bootstrap.dart:364 subscribes connectedClientCountStream and :372 seeds the current value at wire-up, into packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/web_server_provider.dart:219 setConnectedClients; web_server_provider.dart:209 resets it to 0 in setStopped so a stopped server cannot keep claiming viewers. UI: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/widgets/remote_access_settings.dart:534 binds 'Active Viewers' to webState.connectedClients, with a separate 'Co-imaging viewers' row at :537-543 still showing webState.activeViewers, and the status-bar chip follows the same field (session_sharing.dart:22, :73, :122). The two populations are now two rows rather than one mislabelled one.
revert_check: Two severed call sites, run separately. (a) Server: commented out both `_publishConnectedClientCount();` calls at websocket_sessions.dart:82 and :138 => both connected_client_count_test cases FAILED ('a client holding the event stream is counted as connected': Expected contains <1>, Actual []). (b) UI: pointed the Active Viewers row's value back at `webState.activeViewers` (remote_access_settings.dart:534) => 'the collaboration count is not presented as remote clients' FAILED (Found 0 widgets with text '2' under the Active Viewers row). Both restored; 2/2 desktop and 4/4 app green.
caveats: connectedClientCount is the WebSocket registry, so it counts clients holding /events or /api/ws. A client doing only polled REST calls is not 'connected' by this measure -- which matches what the row claims.

title: Filter Focus Offsets silently omits the filter you just added -- you cannot set an offset for it without saving and re-opening the editor
summary: Closed by wave 3/4 (test file dated 2026-08-03 22:21, after the 17:xx re-verification). The verifier's location correction was the accurate one and is what the tree now fixes: the offsets loop is packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/equipment_profiles_screen_parts/profile_details_helpers.dart:155-166 reading _filterControllers[i].text, and the filter-name TextField that had no onChanged is _EditableFilterChip in profile_controls.dart -- not profile_details_rendering.dart:449-500. profile_controls.dart:335 now has `onChanged: (_) => onNameChanged(),` on that field, declared at :311 and required at :316, and the editor supplies it at profile_details_rendering.dart:534 `onNameChanged: () => _update(() {})`. _update is plain setState (profile_details.dart:444) and the controllers live in State fields, so rebuilding on each keystroke does not recreate them or move the caret.
test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/settings/equipment_profile_filter_offset_sync_test.dart -- 2/2 green as found; covers both symptoms the verifier saw (the offsets card not appearing at all for the first filter, and a '+'-added filter having no offset row until save).
revert_check: Severed the production call site at profile_details_rendering.dart:534, `onNameChanged: () => _update(() {})` -> `onNameChanged: () {}` => both cases FAILED ('naming the first filter reveals its focus-offset row at once': Found 0 widgets with text 'Filter Focus Offsets'; 'a filter added with + gets an offset row without saving': expected 2 widgets with text 'Ha', found 1). Restored; 2/2 green.

title: Log Export dumps 18.8 MB into the home Documents folder without warning, ignoring both the configured data directory and the app's own exports/ folder
summary: Closed by wave 3/4 (test file dated 2026-08-03 22:41, after the 17:11:30 repro). The old body built '<Documents>/skotiq_logs_<ts>.txt' and wrote every retained rotated file there unasked. packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/widgets/log_viewer.dart:421-424 now asks _askExportScope first (defined :309, offering 'Entries on screen - N entries, exactly as filtered' vs 'Full history - every retained log file, about <size>'), then :435-437 resolves the destination through logExportTargetPickerProvider, which is chooseExportTarget -- the same native save flow profile export uses (screen_shell.dart:72) -- seeded with defaultLogExportDirectory() (log_viewer.dart:49), the Skotiq/exports directory the app's other exports go to. Cancelling either step returns before any write (:425-429 and :438-442), and the completion message states the bytes actually written (:459-468). The 18 MB dump is now only what 'Full history' does, after the operator picked it and was told the size.
revert_check: Two severed steps, run separately. (a) Replaced the picker call at log_viewer.dart:435 with the original `ExportTarget(path: '${docsDir.path}/skotiq_logs_$timestamp.txt')` => 3 of 4 cases FAILED ('the on-screen scope writes only what the viewer shows', 'the full-history scope is what dumps every rotated file', 'cancelling the destination writes nothing'). (b) Restored that and replaced the `_askExportScope(...)` result at :421 with a hard-coded `const chosen = LogExportScope.fullHistory;` => all 4 FAILED, including 'Export asks what it should contain, and how big that is' (Found 0 widgets with text 'Export logs'). Both restored; 4/4 green.
caveats: 'Full history' still reads the real platform log directory rather than a directory derived from SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR -- that is where LoggingService actually writes, so it is reading the right files, but a sandboxed instance still exports the host's logs. Not the behaviour the title is about (where it WRITES), and I did not change it.

title: Duplicate happily creates two profiles with byte-identical names, while Import de-duplicates -- so the profile list can show rows nothing can tell apart
summary: Closed by wave 3/4 (test file dated 2026-08-03 22:48, after the 17:xx repro that produced five rows all named 'Adv Rig One (Copy)'). The fixed '${profile.name} (Copy)' the verifier found at screen_shell.dart:368 is now packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/equipment_profiles_screen_parts/screen_shell.dart:548 `initialName: uniqueProfileName('${profile.name} (Copy)', takenNames)`, with takenNames read from equipmentProfileListProvider at :543-547. uniqueProfileName (screen_shell.dart:29-37) is the importer's own rule -- keep base if free, else 'base (1)', 'base (2)', ... -- compared through normalizeProfileName (:40, trim + lowercase) so 'My Rig' and 'my rig ' collide, matching the editor's _duplicateNameError. The proposed fix's other half is covered too: the dialog is given takenNames and refuses a hand-typed collision, which the suite asserts separately, so the offered name is not the only thing standing between the operator and two identical rows.
test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/settings/equipment_profile_duplicate_name_test.dart -- 4/4 green as found (2 unit cases on uniqueProfileName incl. case/whitespace, 1 widget case on the second Duplicate's pre-filled name, 1 on a hand-typed collision being refused).
revert_check: Severed the production call site at screen_shell.dart:548, `initialName: uniqueProfileName('${profile.name} (Copy)', takenNames)` -> `initialName: '${profile.name} (Copy)'` => 'the second copy is offered a name no other profile has' FAILED with Expected 'Adv Rig One (Copy) (1)', Actual 'Adv Rig One (Copy)'. Restored; 4/4 green.
caveats: No UNIQUE index was added to equipment_profiles.name -- the finding offered that as an alternative, and both UI paths that can propose a name now resolve collisions, so the schema was left alone.
